entities.summary: Sable Island is an island in the North Atlantic Ocean, about 300 kilometres (160 nmi) southeast of Halifax, Canada, and about 175 kilometres (95 nmi) southeast of the closest point of mainland Nova Scotia. The island is staffed year-round by employees of Canada's National Parks agency, Parks Canada. The number of people on Sable Island fluctuates throughout the year, rising during the summer months when the island is frequented by researchers and an increased staff complement. Notable for its role in early Canadian history and the Sable Island horse, the island is protected and managed by Parks Canada, which must grant permission prior to any visit.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sable Island played a crucial role in early Canadian history as a vital stopover for whales and a site of early European exploration. The island's unique ecosystem and isolation made it an important location for scientific research, with the Sable Island horse being a notable example.
